steps.message:
Create a 16:9, 6-slide data analysis report PPT targeted at engineering leaders, CTOs, and developer experience teams evaluating technology strategy and hiring priorities.

This deck should present a clear narrative about how the programming language landscape is shifting, which languages developers love most, and how language choice maps to application domains. The narrative arc should move from "how usage is changing" -> "what developers actually prefer" -> "what to do about it."

Use the 6 slide titles provided in the `slides` array of `task_input.json` exactly as given, in order.
Slide 2 (Language Trends) must use a line chart or comparison table to show 2017-2024 usage data for at least the top 8 languages.
Slide 4 (Developer Satisfaction) should use a horizontal bar chart to display satisfaction scores for the top 10 languages.
Slide 5 (Domain Specialization) should use a heatmap or structured table showing which language leads each application domain.
Do not fabricate any data or statistics not found in source_brief.md.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > generate_ppt.py
import collections 
import collections.abc
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

def generate_ppt():
    prs = Presentation()
    
    # Set 16:9 aspect ratio
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.33333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    # 1. Title Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    title = slide.shapes.title
    subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]

    title.text = "State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Trends, Satisfaction, and Strategic Shifts"
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(40)
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    
    subtitle.text = "JetBrains' annual survey of 23,262 developers worldwide.\n\nThe most comprehensive snapshot of the developer community, covering languages, tools, AI attitudes, and career trends."
    subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(20)

    # 2. Language Trends Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5] # blank with title
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = "Python Closes the Gap: 8 Years of Language Usage Shifts"

    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
    chart_data.categories = ['2017', '2020', '2022', '2024']
    chart_data.add_series('JavaScript', (65, 70, 65, 61))
    chart_data.add_series('Python', (32, 55, 53, 57))
    chart_data.add_series('HTML/CSS', (60, 61, 54, 51))
    chart_data.add_series('SQL', (42, 56, 49, 48))
    chart_data.add_series('Java', (47, 54, 48, 46))
    chart_data.add_series('TypeScript', (12, 28, 34, 37))
    chart_data.add_series('Go', (8, 19, 19, 18))
    chart_data.add_series('Rust', (0, 7, 9, 11))
    chart_data.add_series('PHP', (30, 27, 20, 17))
    chart_data.add_series('Kotlin', (2, 17, 16, 14))

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11.3), Inches(5.5)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE_MARKERS, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
    ).chart
    chart.has_legend = True
    chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
    
    # 3. Primary Language Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = "Python Is Now the #1 Primary Language at 35%"
    
    tx_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(1.3), Inches(11.3), Inches(0.5))
    tx_box.text = "Contrast primary usage with adoption intent (all below 6%) to illustrate ecosystem lock-in and the comfort zone effect."

    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
    chart_data.categories = ['Python', 'Java', 'JavaScript', 'TypeScript', 'SQL']
    chart_data.add_series('Primary Language (%)', (35, 30, 28, 19, 17))
    chart_data.add_series('Adoption Intent (%)', (6, 4, 0, 5, 4)) # using 0 for unspecified

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(11.3), Inches(5)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
    ).chart
    chart.has_legend = True
    chart.legend.include_in_layout = False

    # 4. Developer Satisfaction Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = "TypeScript and Rust Top Developer Satisfaction, Nearly Tied at 199 vs 198"

    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
    # Reverse order for bar chart to show highest at top if horizontal, but pptx bar chart draws bottom up
    categories = ['C', 'Dart', 'Shell', 'Kotlin', 'C++', 'Lua', 'Go', 'Python', 'Rust', 'TypeScript']
    scores = [86, 93, 100, 113, 113, 118, 129, 151, 198, 199]
    chart_data.categories = categories
    chart_data.add_series('Satisfaction Score', scores)

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11.3), Inches(5.5)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
    ).chart
    chart.has_legend = False

    # 5. Domain Specialization Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = "Each Language Owns a Domain: AI Belongs to Python, UI to TypeScript"

    rows = 8
    cols = 3
    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(2), Inches(2), Inches(9.3), Inches(3.5)
    table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, x, y, cx, cy).table

    # set column widths
    table.columns[0].width = Inches(4)
    table.columns[1].width = Inches(3.3)
    table.columns[2].width = Inches(2)

    headers = ["Domain", "Top Language", "Share"]
    for i, header in enumerate(headers):
        table.cell(0, i).text = header
        
    data = [
        ["AI / Machine Learning", "Python", "31%"],
        ["Data Processing & Analytics", "Python", "17%"],
        ["User Interface", "TypeScript", "62%"],
        ["APIs & Services", "Java", "49%"],
        ["Application Logic & Workflows", "Java", "55%"],
        ["System Tools & Components", "C++", "27%"],
        ["Integrating with APIs & Services", "Python", "38%"]
    ]

    for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data):
        for col_idx, cell_data in enumerate(row_data):
            table.cell(row_idx+1, col_idx).text = cell_data

    # 6. Strategic Takeaways Slide
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    slide.shapes.title.text = "What This Means for Your Technology Strategy in 2025"

    body = slide.placeholders[1]
    tf = body.text_frame
    tf.text = "1. Invest in Python for AI/ML teams — it is the undisputed leader."
    
    p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = "2. TypeScript is the future of frontend and full-stack."
    
    p3 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p3.text = "3. Rust and Go are the growth plays for infrastructure and systems."
    
    p4 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p4.text = "4. PHP and Ruby hiring pools are shrinking."
    
    p5 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p5.text = "5. Developer satisfaction correlates with type safety and modern tooling — factor this into retention strategy."

    for p in tf.paragraphs:
        p.font.size = Pt(24)
        p.space_after = Pt(14)

    import os
    if not os.path.exists('/app/output'):
        os.makedirs('/app/output')
    prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')

generate_ppt()
EOF
python3 generate_ppt.py
